canonical_name: QR factorization theorem family for finite real or complex matrices
category: 其他重要领域 / 数值分析
literal_source_claim_en: An orthogonal-triangular factorization of a matrix.
canonical_statement: Provisional theorem-family scope: a finite real or complex matrix admits an exact QR factorization A = Q * R, with Q orthogonal/unitary or column-orthonormal and R upper triangular or upper trapezoidal; exact field, shape, rank, factor dimensions, normalization, uniqueness, and boundary conventions remain to be source-frozen.
canonical_claim: A = Q * R with a source-approved orthogonal/unitary Q and upper-triangular or upper-trapezoidal R, under source-approved domain and rank conditions.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not fix real versus complex scalars, square versus rectangular matrices, rank or dimension hypotheses, full versus reduced factorization, factor shapes, orthogonal versus unitary convention, triangularity on rectangular indices, diagonal normalization, uniqueness, or degenerate cases. Axler Theorem 7.58 is a strong inspected square full-column-rank source lead but is not cited or independently admitted; choosing its narrower proposition or a broader arbitrary-matrix statement at intake would silently resolve material scope ambiguity.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix finite square or rectangular matrices, real or complex scalars, ordered finite index types, dimension and rank hypotheses, and universe conventions.
conclusion: Open: existence, and perhaps normalized uniqueness, of correctly shaped factors Q and R satisfying exact matrix equality, orthogonal/unitary or column-orthonormal conditions, and upper-triangular or upper-trapezoidal conditions.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a source proposition is accepted; the statement phase must resolve every case in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Axler Theorem 7.58: unique normalized QR for square real or complex matrices with linearly independent columns
arbitrary square real matrices with orthogonal Q and upper-triangular R
full rectangular QR with square Q and upper-trapezoidal R
reduced rectangular QR with column-orthonormal Q and square or trapezoidal R
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero-by-zero, zero-row, zero-column, and one-by-one matrices
wide, tall, square, invertible, and rank-deficient matrices
the zero matrix and zero, repeated, or dependent columns
already triangular, diagonal, orthogonal, or unitary matrices
real matrices embedded in a complex formulation
positive or nonnegative diagonal normalization and uniqueness in singular cases
excluded_substitutions: Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization or orthonormal-basis existence without the exact matrix product
Schur, LU, Cholesky, polar, singular-value, Jordan, or eigendecomposition
the QR eigenvalue algorithm or any approximate numerical residual
a specialized square, invertible, full-rank, real-only, complex-only, or fixed-size result unless source-frozen
a structure or hypothesis storing the desired factors and equality
the catalog's untrusted verified label or discovery probe as proof credit
